title: SIEM shipping: buffering, idempotency, and backpressure controls for audit stream
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a resilient SIEM delivery path for audit events that tolerates transient downstream failures (Splunk/Datadog/SIEMs), applies sensible backpressure, and provides strong operational guarantees while minimizing duplicate events for customers. This ticket implements a resilient shipping adapter that sits in the audit-stream subsystem and covers buffering, retry/backoff policy, idempotency keys, DLQ handling, and runtime knobs for backpressure and memory limits.

Context & Problem:
- Current webhook/connector implementation retries naive HTTP posts and relies on in-memory queues which expose us to message loss or OOM under bursty traffic.
- Customers see duplicate events or missing audit records after connector restarts or broker hiccups.
- Existing related work: ENG-14230 tenant-scoped sinks and ENG-15342 exactly-once sink contracts. This ticket bridges operational gap for third-party SIEM integrations.

Goals:
- Provide at-least-once delivery with controlled duplicate surface area and an optional deduplication window for customers.
- Implement bounded in-memory buffering with spill to persistent store (local disk) when pressure exceeds thresholds.
- Expose backpressure signals to upstream (throttling/429) and autoscaling hints for Dedicated nodes.
- Provide DLQ and replay tooling; surface metrics and alerts for delivery success, spikes, and DLQ growth.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Chose at-least-once + idempotency keys over full exactly-once. Exactly-once requires distributed transactions and higher latency; for external SIEMs we cannot enforce server-side dedup. We will emit stable idempotency keys and provide a deduplication window documented for customers.
- Buffering: use a hybrid in-memory ring buffer (bounded) with an append-only disk-backed spill file per sink. This minimizes memory spikes while preserving order per-tenant when possible.
- Ordering: preserve per-tenant ordering within a batch; across failures we document that ordering may not be strictly preserved. Strict ordering would increase complexity and stall delivery for slow downstream consumers.
- Retry/backoff: implement exponential backoff with jitter, capped retry attempts (configurable), and circuit-breaker to move failing tenants to DLQ after threshold.
- Idempotency: include a canonical id field (sha256 of tenantID + eventID + timestamp-trim) sent as X-Redwood-Idempotency header so receiving SIEMs that support dedup can use it.

Implementation plan & acceptance criteria:
1) Adapter core: buffering API, disk spill, recovery on restart, tests for lossless spill and replay. Acceptance: restart does not lose events for 10k event test.
2) Retry and circuit-breaker: configurable backoff, thresholds per-tenant. Acceptance: simulated 503 returns lead to expected backoff behavior and eventual DLQ after threshold.
3) Idempotency headers: implement header and doc. Acceptance: header set for all outbound HTTP calls and recorded in delivery logs.
4) Metrics & alerts: delivery_success_rate, in_flight_events, dlq_count, avg_delivery_latency, connector_uptime. Acceptance: dashboards added; alert for DLQ growth > 50 events in 5m.
5) Operational tools: replay DLQ per-tenant; manual requeue via Console and a retry API. Acceptance: replay of 100 events successfully processed in staging.

Progress & recent updates:
- 2026-03-02: spike completed — validated spill-to-disk library (benchmark attached in Confluence).
- 2026-03-04: prototype PR opened for buffering layer (https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-connectors/pull/212). Feedback from reliability team requested changes to file rotation.
- 2026-03-07: design review with Security and PM; agreed on idempotency header format and DLQ policy. Action: add a tenant-config knob to opt-out of idempotency header for regulated sinks.
- 2026-03-09: added circuit-breaker and initial metrics. Integration test failing intermittently under high concurrency — root cause suspected race in ack offset persistence.

Open blockers & risks:
- Offset persistence race: needs locking or atomic rename pattern. Risk: duplicate deliveries during rapid restarts. Workaround: increase retry window and communicate to early adopters.
- Customer compatibility: some SIEMs reject unknown headers; we will make idempotency header opt-out and provide SDK docs.
- Memory vs disk thresholds tuning: must be validated on dedicated workloads to avoid excessive disk I/O.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for buffer, spill, and replay.
- Integration tests against local mock SIEM that simulates 429/503/timeout behaviors.
- Load test in staging to validate tail latency and DLQ behavior (script: load-test-audit-siem).
- Chaos tests: connector restart during active bursts.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated by tenant flag. Stage rollout: internal tenants -> beta customers -> GA.
- Monitor metrics and a curated alert runbook.
- Postmortem checklist for any DLQ regressions.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Resilient+SIEM+Shipping+Adapter
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-connectors/pull/212
- Load test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/integration-tests/tree/main/audit-siem-load
- Incident notes from last production delivery issue: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-incident-notes

Next steps (short term):
- Fix offset persistence race (assigned) and add stronger atomic write pattern.
- Complete integration tests and bump estimate if more work required.
- Prepare beta onboarding doc for two pilot customers (security and compliance review required).

Notes from reviewers:
- PM (Lara Mills): prioritize telemetry so SRE can auto-scale Dedicated pools on sustained backlog.
- Security (Omar Reyes): ensure idempotency header cannot leak PII; sanitize inputs before generating keys.
- Reliability (Anika Patel): add per-tenant memory cap and soft-drop policy if tenant exceeds quota (with audit event about drop).

Acceptance criteria (final):
- No data loss in restart/replay tests and integration tests pass for at-least-once semantics.
- Dashboards and alerts in Console for DLQ, delivery rate, and error budget.
- Documentation for customers describing dedup window and idempotency behavior.
notes: Will coordinate rollout with Solutions Engineering and Compliance; schedule security review once offset bug fixed.
